---
title: "Career Strategy"
subtitle: "Turning Our Market Evidence into an Action Plan"
---

## Our Career Decision

Our evidence supports a two-stage career strategy. In the near term, we should
target **Analytics and Data roles** because they align most closely with our
current strengths in SQL, Data Modeling, and Data Visualization. We should
treat **AI/ML Architecture roles** as a longer-term pathway that becomes more
attainable after we strengthen Machine Learning, MLOps, AWS, Generative AI, and
production-oriented Python.

This recommendation does not mean the AI/ML pathway is unattractive. Six of
the 10 audited postings belong to the AI/ML Architecture cluster. However,
these postings are predominantly senior roles and emphasize several skills for
which our current proficiency is below the market-priority benchmark.

## Evidence Behind the Strategy

Our recommendation combines four parts of the project:

1. The [exploratory analysis](eda.qmd) shows that the audited market is small,
   senior-oriented, and concentrated in adjacent AI, ML, architecture, and
   analytics roles.
2. The [skill-gap analysis](skill_gap_analysis.qmd) identifies our largest gap
   in MLOps, followed by Machine Learning. Python, AWS, and Generative AI are
   also high-priority development areas.
3. The [ML analysis](ml_methods.qmd) separates the postings into a six-posting
   AI/ML Architecture cluster and a four-posting Analytics and Data cluster.
4. The [NLP analysis](nlp_methods.qmd) provides a second source of skill
   evidence by comparing explicit description language with Lightcast's
   structured skill fields.

| Decision factor | Analytics and Data pathway | AI/ML Architecture pathway |
|---|---:|---:|
| Audited postings | 4 | 6 |
| Core Data Scientist postings | 1 | 0 |
| Median minimum experience | 5 years | 5 years |
| Usable salary observations | 1 of 4 | 6 of 6 |
| Strongest alignment with our profile | SQL, Data Modeling, Data Visualization | Foundation in Python and technical analysis |
| Largest preparation needs | Python depth and Machine Learning | MLOps, Machine Learning, AWS, Generative AI, production Python |
| Recommended timing | Near-term target | Longer-term stretch pathway |

The reported cluster salaries are not directly comparable. Every AI/ML
Architecture posting reports usable salary information, while only one
Analytics and Data posting does. We therefore do not use the salary difference
as evidence that one pathway pays more than the other.

## Target Role Tiers

### Primary Targets

Our first search tier should emphasize entry-level or early-career versions of
the Analytics and Data pathway:

- Data Analyst
- Business Intelligence Analyst
- Junior Analytics Engineer
- Junior Data Scientist
- Customer or Product Analytics Analyst

The audited postings themselves are mostly senior positions. These primary
titles are therefore role-family search targets, not a claim that the current
10-posting panel contains entry-level openings.

### Secondary Targets

After completing stronger portfolio evidence, we can expand the search to:

- Data Scientist
- Analytics Engineer
- Machine Learning Analyst
- Applied Data Scientist
- Decision Scientist

### Longer-Term Targets

The following roles should remain stretch goals until we can demonstrate
production and cloud skills:

- Machine Learning Engineer
- MLOps Engineer
- Applied Scientist
- AI Solution Architect
- AI or ML Enterprise Architect

## Our 90-Day Development Plan

| Period | Skill focus | Planned work | Evidence we will produce |
|---|---|---|---|
| Days 1–30 | Python, SQL, Data Modeling, and Data Visualization | Refactor the market-analysis workflow into reusable data preparation and analysis components. | Reproducible scripts, validation checks, a documented data model, and an analytical dashboard |
| Days 31–60 | Machine Learning and MLOps | Build and evaluate an ML workflow, track experiments, and document model limitations. | Model comparison, validation metrics, MLflow experiment records, and a model card |
| Days 61–90 | AWS, deployment, and Generative AI | Package one project, deploy a small cloud demonstration, and extend the NLP skill extractor. | Docker configuration, cloud architecture diagram, deployed demonstration, and an evaluated NLP feature |

We will not increase a proficiency rating solely because a course was
completed. A rating should increase only when we can demonstrate the skill in
a reproducible artifact and explain the decisions made during development.

## Portfolio Strategy

### Project 1: Job-Market Analytics Product

We will develop the current analysis into a polished portfolio case study. It
will demonstrate data cleaning, SQL-style transformations, exploratory
analysis, Plotly visualization, and responsible interpretation of missing
data. The published Quarto website will serve as the primary communication
artifact.

### Project 2: Reproducible ML Workflow

We will convert the clustering work into a documented ML workflow containing
feature construction, model selection, diagnostic measures, and limitations.
We will then add experiment tracking and packaging so the project demonstrates
MLOps concepts rather than only notebook-based modeling.

### Project 3: Job-Description Skill Extractor

We will extend the NLP analysis into a small application that accepts job text,
identifies skills, and compares them with our current profile. The application
should report the evidence behind each match and avoid presenting its results
as an automated hiring decision.

## Application Strategy

We will use the following process once the first portfolio project is ready:

1. Search primarily for early-career Analytics and Data titles while tracking
   AI/ML openings as longer-term market signals.
2. Tailor each resume version to skills that are supported by our projects; we
   will not list unverified proficiency claims.
3. Link applications to the most relevant portfolio artifact rather than using
   the same project description for every role.
4. Record the title, employer, required skills, application date, response,
   and interview stage.
5. Review results after every 20 targeted applications and revise our title
   filters, resume language, or portfolio evidence when response rates remain
   weak.

## Collaboration and Documentation

We will manage the remaining work through GitHub issues, named task owners,
documented commits, and short weekly status records. Each completed task should
identify its source data, method, output, and reviewer. This makes the workflow
reproducible and preserves clear evidence of individual contributions while
the website presents a unified Group 10 analysis.

## Measures of Progress

We will evaluate the plan using evidence rather than course completion alone:

| Measure | 90-day target |
|---|---:|
| Fully documented portfolio case studies | 2 |
| Cloud-deployed demonstrations | 1 |
| Projects with automated validation checks | 2 |
| Projects with reproducible environment instructions | 2 |
| Targeted applications reviewed as one decision cycle | 20 |
| Updated skill assessments supported by artifacts | At least 3 skills |

## Risks and Adjustments

Our market evidence is based on only 10 audited postings from one industry and
time window. It is also heavily weighted toward senior roles. We should retain
the defined project scope for analytical consistency but avoid treating this
sample as the complete employment market. Before beginning a broad application
campaign, we should compare our target titles with a larger and more recent set
of entry-level postings.

If the larger search confirms that analytics roles remain more attainable, we
will continue the staged plan. If entry-level ML roles show materially greater
availability and align with our completed portfolio evidence, we can move the
AI/ML pathway forward without changing the standards used to assess readiness.

## Final Recommendation

Our recommended immediate pathway is **Analytics and Data**, supported by
portfolio evidence in SQL, Python, Data Modeling, and Data Visualization. Our
recommended long-term pathway is **AI/ML Architecture and Engineering**, with
advancement conditioned on demonstrable improvement in Machine Learning,
MLOps, cloud deployment, and Generative AI.

This staged strategy preserves an ambitious destination while grounding our
next decision in the skills we can currently demonstrate.
